clue.text: Local round state associated primarily with India?

definitions.text: Local round state associated primarily with India?

indicators.note: round means going around, so the pub's letters enclose the state

parts.note: a local is a British pub, the drinking place nearest home
NJ is the abbreviation for New Jersey, a US state

indicators.note: primarily asks for the leading letter of the word associated

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about which state round here is mainly linked with India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is British slang for the nearest pub. Read as a whole, the clue also describes the answer: a local of a state in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A person native to Punjab, a state of northern India, is a local of that region.

clue.text: Food taken before evidence of sleep for vitality

indicators.note: taken before means coming first, ahead of the next piece

parts.note: a pizza is a type of food
ZZ represents snoring in cartoons, showing someone is asleep

explanation.surface: Eating before signs of dozing off gives energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pizzazz is lively flair and energy, which is vitality.

clue.text: One from country forgetful of time showing innocence

indicators.note: forgetful of means leaving out, so a letter disappears

parts.note: a native is someone born in a particular country

explanation.surface: A country dweller who loses track of time looks guileless.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means artless and unworldly, lacking experience, which shows innocence.

clue.text: Make worse government in Indian city with tax on energy

indicators.note: in means placed inside the city's letters

parts.note: Agra is a city in India, home of the Taj Mahal
VAT is value added tax
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Rule in an Indian city, with a tax on power, makes things worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'on' just join the pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggravate a problem is to intensify it, which is to make it worse.

clue.text: Distinctive tongue having origin of old in northerly part of France

indicators.note: in means placed inside the reversed region
northerly in a down clue means going upwards, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: the Midi is the south of France

indicators.note: origin of asks for the first letter of the word old

explanation.surface: A regional dialect has old roots in the north of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northerly' looks like geography, but in a down clue it turns MIDI, the south of France, upward into IDIM.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a form of expression or dialect peculiar to a people or place.

clue.text: Person with strict taste in Indian food cheers starter of nan

parts.note: puri is a deep-fried Indian bread
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

indicators.note: starter of points to the opening letter of the word nan

explanation.surface: Someone fussy about curry house fare thanks the waiter as the naan bread arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: A puritan is someone with rigid moral or aesthetic standards, hence a person of strict taste.

clue.text: Bring up work on book penned by one working hard? It's a lucrative one

indicators.note: bring up in a down clue means lift, so the letters read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed within, so the letters go inside

parts.note: a toiler is someone who works hard

explanation.surface: A hard-working writer brings out a book that earns money.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Bring up' reads a piece upwards; 'one' in the definition refers back to the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A potboiler is a book or artwork made quickly just to earn money, so a work done for profit.

clue.text: A principal rule coming foremost for religious follower

indicators.note: coming foremost means moving to the front, so that letter is shifted to the start

parts.note: a star is the principal performer

explanation.surface: A main principle comes first for a believer.
explanation.walkthrough: In A STAR, 'coming foremost' takes the final R to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rasta, or Rastafarian, follows a religion revering Haile Selassie of Ethiopia.

clue.text: Case negotiated by eight possibly, we hear, in major way

parts.note: a trunk is a large travelling case

indicators.note: we hear means the word is caught by ear, giving a word said the same way

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew, so water negotiated by it is rowed

explanation.surface: Luggage carried along a main route by a team, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eight' is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A trunk road is a main highway in Britain, one of the major routes.

clue.text: Like some trains showing refusal after tip-off to carry tons for construction

indicators.note: to carry means holding inside, so the shortened refusal wraps the other letters
after tip-off means once the tip is cut off, the last letter goes

parts.note: nope is a slang refusal

indicators.note: for construction means for building anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone refuses, after a warning, to haul heavy loads for a building job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip-off' looks like a warning, but it means the tip of the slang refusal is cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: Express trains run between termini without stopping at stations in between.

clue.text: Spot around Eastern point imbued with European spirit of the period

indicators.note: around means the spot's letters go round the Eastern letter

parts.note: a zit is a pimple, a spot on the skin

indicators.note: imbued with means filled with, so the point's letters take the European letter inside

parts.note: the gist is the main point of something

explanation.surface: Pinpointing a dot on an Eastern map, steeped in Europe, captures the age.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeitgeist is a German borrowing meaning the defining mood or outlook of an era.

clue.text: Avoid one in jacket getting snubbed before service

indicators.note: snubbed here means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a spud is a potato, which may be baked in its jacket
RN is the Royal Navy, often called the senior service

explanation.surface: Someone in a jacket is cold-shouldered before a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in jacket' seems to be a person wearing a coat, but it is a jacket potato. 'getting snubbed' trims SPUD to SPU.
explanation.definitionFit: To spurn something is to reject or shun it, which is to avoid it scornfully.

clue.text: Payment mostly pocketed by reformist group in stadium

indicators.note: pocketed by means held inside the group's letters

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, a group helping drinkers reform

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: rent is a regular payment for property

explanation.surface: A campaign group has quietly kept most of the fee for a sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformist group' is Alcoholics Anonymous, whose members reform their drinking, not a political faction.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a large venue for sport or spectacle, the same kind of place as a stadium.

clue.text: Sort of coat make worn by leader in Jinan?

definitions.text: Sort of coat make worn by leader in Jinan?

indicators.note: worn by means wrapped around, so the rearranged letters surround the leading letter
sort of here means to sort, putting the letters into a new order
leader in asks for the first letter of the word Jinan

explanation.surface: Asks what kind of coat a party chief in the Chinese city of Jinan would wear.
explanation.walkthrough: Jinan is a city in China. The whole clue also describes the garment, worn by Chairman Mao, so it works as definition and wordplay at once.
explanation.definitionFit: This high-collared tunic jacket was popularised by Chairman Mao and became standard dress across China.

clue.text: Wine with a lot of spirit found by enthusiast was premier sort on reflection

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: zing means energy or liveliness, a kind of spirit
a fan is an enthusiast

indicators.note: on reflection means seen in a mirror, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: led means was first or ahead, i.e. was premier

explanation.surface: A glass with plenty of liquor, found by a keen drinker who rated it the top kind on thinking it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims ZING to ZIN; 'on reflection' turns LED into DEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Zinfandel is a red grape variety grown widely in California and the wine made from it.

clue.text: What could be cultivated for profit instead of degree among geeks producing tension?

indicators.note: instead of means one thing takes another's place within the geeks' letters

parts.note: nerds are geeks

parts.words: What could be cultivated for profit
parts.note: vines are grown commercially for grapes and wine

explanation.surface: Swotty types consider farming for cash rather than a degree, and it causes stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instead of degree among geeks' puts VINES where D is in NERDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerviness is a state of nervous strain, a jittery tension.

clue.text: Falsify a note in academic achievement

parts.note: to doctor figures is to falsify them
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Faking a mark on a degree certificate.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctorate is the highest university degree, a peak of scholarly attainment.

clue.text: Vessel in popular competition making comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the pools are the football pools, a popular British betting competition on match results

explanation.surface: A boat appears in a well-known contest that is returning to the schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: The football pools are a long-running British weekly bet on football results.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloop is a single-masted sailing boat, one kind of vessel.

clue.text: One labouring for the Prince of Wales?

definitions.text: One labouring for the Prince of Wales?

parts.words: One labouring for the Prince of Wales?
parts.note: the Prince of Wales is also a London theatre, so a worker there handles scenery

explanation.surface: Someone toiling in the service of the heir to the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal reading misleads: the Prince of Wales Theatre is in London's West End.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre's scenery and props are moved by such a backstage worker, who labours for the theatre.

clue.text: Analyse Zoroastrian descendant with no end of pedigree

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a Parsee is a member of the Zoroastrian community descended from Persians who settled in India

indicators.note: end of asks for the final letter of the word pedigree

explanation.surface: Tracing the ancestry of a Zoroastrian whose family tree lacks a conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' pedigree is E, which 'with no' takes from PARSEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To parse a sentence is to break it into its grammatical parts, a form of analysis.

clue.text: Historic plant raised for chemist

parts.note: historic means belonging to the past

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means lifted upward, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: rue is a bitter herb

explanation.surface: An old herb is cultivated for a pharmacist.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was a French chemist who pioneered pasteurisation and vaccines.

clue.text: A diner getting excited in the wake of my spicy stuff

indicators.note: in the wake of means following, so the exclamation comes first and the rest follows

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!

indicators.note: getting excited means stirred up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A restaurant customer gets worked up after exclaiming at a hot dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is not a possessive but an exclamation of surprise, matched by the British 'cor!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coriander is an aromatic herb whose seeds and leaves flavour curries, so it is a spice.

clue.text: Followers in English element blocking Napoleon's way

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the middle of, so these letters go inside

parts.note: rue is French for street, Napoleon being French
tin is a chemical element

explanation.surface: Supporters in an English material obstructing the Emperor's route.
explanation.definitionFit: A retinue is a group of attendants accompanying an important person.

clue.text: Tell maybe part that's been picked up in cake?

parts.note: William Tell is a Swiss folk hero, an example of someone Swiss

indicators.note: picked up means caught by the ear, so the word for part is replaced by one said the same

parts.note: a role is a part played by an actor

explanation.surface: William Tell's role is overheard inside a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell' looks like a verb but is William Tell, the Swiss archer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss roll is a sponge cake spread with jam and rolled into a cylinder.

clue.text: Rumour from oddly scary note

indicators.note: oddly asks for the first, third and fifth letters of the word scary

parts.note: so (soh) is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Gossip comes from a strangely frightening message.
explanation.definitionFit: A say-so is an unsupported assertion, hearsay of the sort rumour spreads.

clue.text: Porky around front of tum needing hospital? Yes and no!

indicators.note: around means wrapped round, so the slang word's letters surround the rest

parts.note: porky is short for pork pie, Cockney rhyming slang for a lie

indicators.note: front of asks for the first letter of the word tum

explanation.surface: A fat man with a big belly needs hospital treatment, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porky' suggests a fat person, but it is rhyming slang. The wordplay suggests a plump figure needing care; the answer means slim and supple, so the clue is both yes and no.
explanation.definitionFit: A lithe body is supple and pliant, able to bend either way, much like an answer of both yes and no.

clue.text: Fund-raising activity, say, with online outlet

parts.note: E stands for electronic, as in email, so online
a vent is an opening that lets air or gas out, an outlet

explanation.surface: A charity drive combined with a web-based shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A fund-raising activity such as a gala or sponsored walk is an example of an organised occasion.

clue.text: Crates hermetically sealed in Surrey town

indicators.note: sealed in means held inside these words, so the town sits within them

explanation.surface: Packing cases are airtight in a commuter town.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county just south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Esher is a town in the English county of Surrey, near Kingston.

clue.text: Old comic with regal figure replacing male in TV award

indicators.note: replacing means one piece stands in for another in the award's letters

parts.note: an Emmy is an American television award
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A veteran comedian is given a TV prize, with royalty taking over from a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' swaps one M in EMMY for ER. Dick Emery was a British TV comedian of the 1960s and 70s.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick Emery was a British comedian famous for his sketch-show characters, now a figure of the past.

clue.text: Fabric star sported when beset by E Morales' rival?

indicators.note: when beset by means surrounded by, so the rival's letters enclose the rearranged ones

parts.note: Amir Khan, A Khan by initial and surname, is a British boxer and a possible opponent for the Mexican boxer Erik Morales, given here as E Morales

indicators.note: sported in the sense of a plant sport, a mutation, so the letters change their order

explanation.surface: A celebrity wears cloth while hemmed in by a boxer's opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxer is given by initial and surname, mirroring the E of E Morales, the Mexican boxer Erik Morales.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrakhan is a fabric with a curled pile imitating the fleece of young Karakul lambs.

clue.text: Retired gentleman taken with fish and fried food

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: sir is the address for a gentleman
sole is a flatfish

explanation.surface: An elderly man eating fish and a fry-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A rissole is a cake of minced meat coated in breadcrumbs and fried.

clue.text: Actress in principle shunning outsiders is back

indicators.note: in means placed within the shortened principle
shunning outsiders means the first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: a tenet is a principle or belief
Diana Dors was a British film actress of the 1950s

explanation.surface: A film star, principled but shunning outsiders, is returning.
explanation.walkthrough: Diana Dors was a British screen actress of the 1950s. 'back' looks like part of the story but is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse is to support or approve, as to back a candidate.
